answer: Persistent work trail. Each agent identity accumulates a signed, append-only ledger of solved tasks; the protocol samples across the population the way a plume disperses through an ocean, requiring any new identity to reproduce the historical trail depth of its neighborhood. Duplicates surface because a copy must re-run or forge prior work, and sampling spans a canyon of task histories that cannot be backfilled cheaply. Attacker cost: replaying each cloned identity's full trail, paying compute per clone rather than per operator.
